input: A finite three-dimensional point set S and a valid tetrahedral triangulation DT_k.
state: Tetrahedra, facet adjacency, a containing tetrahedron, and remaining insertion points.
update: For p in S, find the containing cell, collect C={tetrahedra whose circumspheres contain p}, and set DT_(k+1)=(DT_k minus C) union B, where B cones the cavity boundary to p.
readout: Updated empty-circumsphere tetrahedralization of the inserted vertices.
constraints: The displayed kernel inserts inside the existing domain; initialization needs four noncoplanar vertices. Degenerate predicates and exterior handling are separate implementation details.

input: A finite point set in R^d.
state: A simplicial convex hull with oriented facet equations, neighboring facets, and a disjoint outside-point assignment.
update: Choose a farthest outside point p. Delete facets visible from p, join p to horizon ridges, and repartition the deleted facets outside sets among new facets; discard points below all new facets.
constraints: The formal presentation assumes general position. A facet signed distance is n dot p + b; positive distance denotes visibility. Floating-point facet merging is beyond this card.

input: A running asynchronous process network with directed message channels.
state: Each process local snapshot, each incoming channel message sequence, and marker flags.
update: After recording its local state, a process sends a marker on every outgoing channel before later application messages. First-marker receipt records local state and an empty state for that incoming channel. Other channels record messages received after the local recording and before their marker.
readout: A collection of process states and in-transit channel states forming a consistent global snapshot.
constraints: Error-free FIFO channels; eventual marker delivery. Every process must initiate or be reachable from an initiator for termination. No shared physical clock is required.

input: Process-local event sequences with message sends and receives.
state: A scalar counter C_i per process and a timestamp on each message.
update: Increment C_i between successive local events. Sending attaches the current timestamp T_m. Receipt advances C_i to exceed both its previous value and T_m; integers permit C_i := max(C_i,T_m)+1.
readout: Timestamps satisfying a precedes b implies C(a)<C(b); process identifiers may break equal timestamp ties for total order.
constraints: The implication is one-way: ordered scalar timestamps do not establish causality. No physical-clock synchronization is assumed.

input: A diffusing computation initiated by an environment message through a gate.
state: Per-edge message-minus-signal deficits, outgoing deficit total D, and a cornet of predecessor occurrences of size C.
update: Sending a computation message increments D; receiving its reverse signal decrements D. Receiving a message adds its predecessor to the cornet. Return a signal by deleting that predecessor occurrence subject to the oldest-entry restriction and preserving C>0 or D=0.
readout: A completion signal to the environment when all distributed message obligations have discharged.
constraints: The oldest cornet occurrence is removed only when it is the sole entry. Signals acknowledge computation obligations rather than physical time; OCR notation is not treated as an exact mathematical transcription.

input: A finite simplicial complex with simplices ordered so each prefix is a subcomplex.
state: Cycle representatives indexed by positive simplices and the current boundary relations.
update: Insert simplices in filtration order. A positive simplex creates a homology class; a negative simplex kills a class by making it a boundary, and is paired with a surviving positive simplex using the cycle basis.
readout: Birth/death simplex pairs and intervals; time persistence is death filtration value minus birth filtration value.
constraints: Use a fixed coefficient convention, here mod 2 as a card specialization. An unpaired birth survives to the end. The source index convention subtracts one from index difference and is distinct from real-valued lifetime.

input: A data set X, a filter f:X to Z, a finite cover {U_alpha} of f(X), and a local clustering rule.
state: For each alpha, clusters of f^(-1)(U_alpha); membership lists shared across overlapping cover elements.
update: Pull back the cover, cluster within each inverse image, make a vertex for each cluster, and insert a simplex for a family of clusters with nonempty common intersection.
readout: The nerve complex of the clustered cover, or its graph of pairwise overlaps.
constraints: Cover resolution, overlap, filter, and clustering are explicit parameters. Local clusters can share observations across cover elements; this does not force global cluster disjointness.

input: A finite sequence V_1,...,V_n of finite-dimensional vector spaces with a linear map in either direction between adjacent spaces.
state: Vector-space bases and the directed linear maps of the sequence.
update: Decompose the sequence representation into interval summands I(b_j,d_j), with a one-dimensional space on indices b_j through d_j and zero outside, and identity maps inside each interval.
readout: The multiset Pers(V)={[b_j,d_j]}, invariant under the choice of interval decomposition.
constraints: A field and finite dimensions are required. Both forward and backward maps are allowed. Intervals here are closed integer intervals, unlike the half-open real intervals often used for monotone filtrations. This card states the formal decomposition, not an uninspected update algorithm.

input: A discretized linear problem A_h x_h=b_h and a hierarchy of coarser grids.
state: Fine-grid approximation, coarse-grid projected problems, and transfer operators.
update: Pre-smooth high-frequency error; restrict the remaining problem to a coarser grid and solve recursively; interpolate the correction back and post-smooth. A linear correction formulation is r_h=b_h-A_h x_h, A_H e_H=R r_h, x_h:=x_h+P e_H.
readout: An updated fine-grid approximate solution after descent and ascent through the grid hierarchy.
constraints: The displayed residual equations specialize the source projected-problem description to linear correction form. Coarsening stops where a direct solve is feasible. Grid hierarchy, smoother, restriction R, and interpolation P must be specified by an implementation.

input: A real symmetric matrix A and a nonzero initial vector q_1.
state: Orthogonal basis vectors and tridiagonal coefficients alpha_j,beta_j.
update: Normalize q_1. With beta_0=0, compute w=A q_j-beta_(j-1) q_(j-1), alpha_j=q_j^T w, w:=w-alpha_j q_j, beta_j=||w||_2, and q_(j+1)=w/beta_j if beta_j is nonzero.
readout: A tridiagonal projection T_m=Q_m^T A Q_m; its eigenvalues approximate those of A.
constraints: This card uses normalized modern notation for the symmetric three-term recurrence. Exact arithmetic gives orthogonality; finite precision can lose it. A zero beta is termination, not a division to execute.

input: A nonsymmetric system Ax=b, an initial x, a fixed shadow residual r_tilde, and an invertible preconditioner M.
state: Residual r, search direction p, matrix image v, and scalars rho,alpha,omega.
update: Set rho=r_tilde^T r, beta=(rho/rho_old)(alpha_old/omega_old), p=r+beta(p_old-omega_old v_old); solve M p_hat=p; v=A p_hat; alpha=rho/(r_tilde^T v); s=r-alpha v. Solve M s_hat=s; t=A s_hat; omega=(t^T s)/(t^T t); x:=x+alpha p_hat+omega s_hat and r:=s-omega t. The first iteration uses p=r.
readout: An approximate solution and residual norm after stabilized short-recurrence updates.
constraints: Stop early when s is sufficiently small before the second correction. Zero rho, zero omega, or vanishing denominators require algorithmic breakdown handling. No full Arnoldi basis is stored.
